feedback.problem:
Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of ${x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$

${x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,\frac{{x}^{8}}{720}+⋯$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard Maclaurin expansion for $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{6!}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{24}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{720}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, to get an expansion for ${x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we multiply the above expansion by ${x}^{2}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ={x}^{2}(1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{24}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{720}+⋯) \\  & ={x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{6}}{24}-\frac{{x}^{8}}{720}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
